name: Thunderfang Wolf
lore: It runs ahead of every storm, howling to call the lightning down and then racing it home. Its fur stands on end in a permanent bristle, and its fangs hold a charge long after the sky has gone quiet. It has never been struck, which it interprets as a standing invitation.

Fangs glow like charged copper, eyes bright electric blue, a collar of static fuzz around the neck. It lopes forward mid-stride, jaws parted in a silent howl, paws leaving scorch prints. name: Mushroom Back Turtle
lore: A single vast mushroom grows from its shell, older than the turtle and, some say, in charge. Spores drift from it in slow gold clouds, and whatever they settle on grows a little too well. It walks the damp forest floor like a mobile, patient garden.
design: A squat earth turtle whose shell is buried beneath one enormous mushroom, a broad vermilion cap with pale gills and a spotted white stalk rising from moss-covered plates. The turtle is serene and slow, stubby legs sinking into wet leaves as spores drift in shafts of light. name: Razor Leaf
lore: It is a single leaf that decided it would rather be a blade. It drifts on the wind, catching light on green edges sharp enough to draw blood, and it remembers every hand that has tried to pick it. Meadows whisper about it in their own green way.
design: A floating leaf-creature shaped like a long curved blade of vivid green, its edges gleaming razor-thin, veins running down its length like a spine. A pair of small dark eyes and trailing thin stems give it a watchful face. A thin haze of drifting leaf-litter follows it. name: Rock Troll
lore: It is not made of stone; it simply carries so much of the mountain on its back that the difference stopped mattering. It sleeps under bridges and charges a toll of riddles, and it is not very good at riddles. Few travelers complain, because the alternative is the boulder.
design: A hulking brute of a troll, grey granite plates for skin, a hunched back crusted with boulders and moss, a heavy jaw with blunt tusks and small suspicious eyes. Enormous fists drag near the ground and one shoulder sprouts a tiny tree. name: Knuckle Monkey
lore: It walks on its fists because its arms grew too heavy to do anything else. Its knuckles are callused into stone and it settles every argument by punching the nearest tree. The tree usually loses.

name: Horned Beaver
lore: It sharpened its teeth on a riverbed of iron and grew horns to match. Its dams hold back more than water: whole seasons pool behind them, and the forest downstream has forgotten what spring felt like. It is a patient builder and a terrible neighbor.
design: A stocky beaver with curling ram-like horns of dark iron, its flat tail ridged like a shield and its incisors capped in ore. Fur is dense brown over a broad, low body, paws tipped with flint claws. It stands braced on a half-built dam, shoulders squared, eyes small and stubborn.
